subject: marathon runner
title: The 1904 Olympic Marathon Was Won on Strychnine and Brandy

scenes.text: The 1904 Olympic marathon was won on strychnine and brandy.
St. Louis, 90 degrees, dusty roads, and one well for water, at halfway.
The first man into the stadium had ridden about ten miles in a car. He nearly got the gold.
The real leader was fading, so his trainers dosed him with strychnine, egg white and brandy.
He hallucinated, lost eight pounds, and was held up across the line.
Fourth place: a Cuban in street clothes who stopped for rotten apples and a nap. Of 32 starters, 14 finished.

description:
The 1904 Olympic marathon was won by a man dosed with strychnine and brandy.
The race was run in St. Louis on 30 August 1904 in about 90 F (32 C) heat on dusty roads, and the only water for the runners was a well near the halfway mark. Fred Lorz crossed the line first, but he had dropped out after nine miles and ridden in a car until it broke down; he was about to be awarded the gold medal when spectators objected. The actual winner, Thomas Hicks, was given several doses of strychnine mixed with brandy and egg white by his trainers, hallucinated on the course and was supported across the line in 3:28:53, eight pounds lighter. Andarin Carvajal of Cuba ran in cut-off street clothes, ate rotten apples, took a nap and still came fourth. Of 32 starters, 14 finished.
Which part is the hardest to believe? Comment below.
first_comment: The man who took the car ride was banned for life, got it reduced, then won the 1905 Boston Marathon fairly. Which part is hardest to believe?
